text: Three primary components constitute each Transformer layer: the multi-head self-attention mechanism, which enables the model to weigh the importance of different input positions using query, key, and value projection matrices with quadratic computational complexity in sequence length; the feed-forward network, which enhances representations through position-wise transformations typically expanding the hidden dimension by 4× before projecting back; and embedding layers that map tokens to continuous representations and hidden states to vocabulary probabilities.
note: Qualitative architecture description.

text: In a typical 7B parameter model with 32 layers, hidden dimension 4096, and 32 attention heads, attention mechanisms account for approximately 33% of parameters, feed-forward networks constitute 66%, and embeddings represent the remaining 1%.
note: Per layer: attention 33.2%, FFN 66.8%. Of total 6.74B: attention 31.9%, FFN 64.3%, embeddings ~3.9%. Say "per layer" or use totals.

text: The memory footprint comprises four components: model parameters (28GB for 7B in FP32), matching-size gradients (28GB), optimizer states storing momentum and variance estimates for AdamW (56GB, effectively doubling parameter storage), and activations retained for backpropagation (10–20GB depending on batch size and sequence length).
note: 28+28+56=112 GB (FP32 framing) equals 16 bytes/param mixed-precision total; state which accounting is used.

text: The total requirement of roughly 100–120GB far exceeds consumer GPU capacity and challenges even professional hardware like NVIDIA A100 GPUs with 40–80GB memory.
note: OK; 100-120GB range from Phase 5.

text: A bottleneck of 64 in a model with hidden dimension 4096 requires only 0.5–1% additional parameters, though the sequential nature introduces inference latency.
note: 0.5% at b=64 with two adapters per layer; "0.5-1%" upper bound unsupported. Houlsby report 3.6% on BERT (bigger relative bottleneck).

text: AdaLoRA (Zhang et al., 2023) recognizes that uniform rank across weight matrices is suboptimal and uses importance-based pruning, achieving 30–50% parameter reduction while maintaining accuracy.
note: No 30-50% reduction reported. Paper compares at matched budgets: ~1.3M params, AdaLoRA 89.31 vs LoRA 88.34 GLUE avg; ~0.3M, 88.86 vs 88.15.

text: VeRA (Kopiczko et al., 2024) takes an opposing approach, sharing random matrices across layers and learning only per-layer scaling vectors for 90% parameter reduction at 1–2% accuracy cost.
note: Not "90%/1-2% cost". GLUE: ~7x (RoBERTa-base, 0.3M->0.043M) and ~13x (RoBERTa-large) fewer params, avg -1.4 / 0.0 pts. Instruction tuning: ~100x fewer (Llama 7B 159.9M->1.6M), MT-Bench -0.26 to +0.16.

text: LoRA+ (Hayou et al., 2024) demonstrates that the A and B matrices play asymmetric roles; setting B's learning rate 10–20× higher accelerates convergence by 1.5–2×, suggesting standard LoRA underutilizes its parameter budget due to optimization inefficiency.
note: Ratio: ~2^4=16 for RoBERTa, ~2-4 for Llama-7B (not 10-20x). Speed: up to ~2x. Accuracy: 1-2% improvement. Remove interpretive clause or mark as interpretation.

text: DoRA (Liu et al., 2024) explicitly decomposes updates into magnitude and directional components, closing 50–70% of the gap between LoRA and full fine-tuning, indicating the low-rank assumption itself is not the primary bottleneck.
note: No "50-70% of gap" claim; Table 1 has no full FT row. Report +3.7 (LLaMA-7B), +1.0 (13B), +2.1 (LLaMA2-7B), +4.4 (LLaMA3-8B) pts avg over LoRA at ~equal params (0.84% vs 0.83%).

text: QLoRA (Dettmers et al., 2023) represents a breakthrough in accessibility by combining quantization with low-rank adaptation, quantizing the frozen base model to 4-bit precision while maintaining full-precision LoRA adapters.
note: Qualitative; correct.

text: NormalFloat 4-bit (NF4) assigns quantization levels according to normal distribution quantiles, placing more bins where weights concentrate and fewer in tails, reducing quantization error by 30–40% versus uniform quantization.
note: No "30-40% quantization error" figure. Table 2: Pile CC perplexity NF4+DQ 27.41 vs Int4 34.34 vs FP4 31.07/29.48.

text: Double quantization applies a second pass to the quantization scaling factors themselves, recovering approximately 0.37 bits per parameter (roughly 3GB for a 65B model).
note: 0.373 bits/param, ~3 GB for 65B. Correct.
